sources.entry: Meme Search - AI-powered meme search engine. Automatically extracts descriptions from images using vision-language models, then indexes with vector embeddings for semantic and keyword search. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hostable meme search engine that uses vision-language models to generate descriptions of your images and indexes them with embeddings for semantic and keyword search.
summary.what_it_does: Meme Search scans meme image directories and generates text descriptions with a local image-to-text model (Florence-2, SmolVLM, or Moondream2 variants) or an OpenAI-compatible vision API. Descriptions are stored in Postgres with pgvector, enabling vector and keyword search. The web app supports manual description editing, tags, directory-path filtering, bulk description generation, and directory rescans. Drag-and-drop upload accepts JPG, PNG, WEBP, and GIF files, with up to 50 files per bulk upload. A read-only, token-authenticated /api/v1 search API, a Python CLI, and an experimental Chromium popup are also included. The stack runs under Docker Compose with Rails, a Solid Queue worker, and a Python generator service.
use_cases: Search a personal meme collection by what is in the image
Self-host a semantic image search for a folder of pictures
Organize memes with tags and subdirectory filters
Query a meme library from a terminal via the CLI
Run image captioning with a local vision model without cloud calls
how_to_run: Open the web app on port 3000 (bound to 127.0.0.1 by default)
notable: Local-first: image-to-text and embeddings run on your machine by default
Optional OpenAI-compatible vision API for description generation, with embeddings and search kept local
Read-only /api/v1 search API with scoped bearer tokens, plus a Python CLI
Multiple selectable vision-language models, including an INT8 quantized Moondream2 for lower memory use
Animated GIFs stay animated in display; descriptions use the first frame
caveats: Web UI has no user authentication; official support is loopback-only and public exposure is unsupported
First description generation downloads model weights and is slow
Linux users may need an extra_hosts entry for container networking
